children: , the integrated oil, gas and liquefied-natural-gas heavyweight, grabbed two new offshore bets while its shares traded at $92.96. The company will acquire 30% of BP's Conifer exploration prospect in the Gulf of Mexico and 50% of the Tupinamba block in Brazil's Santos Basin.

BP keeps the operating wheel. Shell gets exposure to potentially valuable acreage without carrying the daily operating burden. But these are prospects, not producing assets. Drilling must hit, the geology must hold up and management must approve development before either stake delivers reserves or cash flow.

Shell's latest quarterly results generated roughly $21.4 billion in operating cash flow and $17.5 billion in free cash flow, providing serious firepower for selective exploration. The stock's $92.96 price sits 12.82% above its $82.40 GF Value estimate, showing that investors already demand strong execution. Shell bought two shots at offshore upsidenot two guaranteed gushers.

title: Shell Buys 30% of BP's Conifer Prospect--Before Any Oil Exists
